agent_priors_used: General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a benchmark comparison is non-identifying unless both a live treatment arm AND non-ceiling baselines exist; measuring per-task economics before the treatment is shipped and the baselines are discriminating yields degenerate or invalid results, so prerequisite repair must precede the flagship run.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): autonomous research lanes drift toward local optima, repeatedly refining a locally measurable instrument while the central decision stays unmade; a concentration/tunnel flag is diagnostic context, never a quota.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): small CPU-quantized LLMs frequently fail structured tool/action emission and multi-step control; supplying the task goal/schema in the system prompt is a known determinant of early-step failure, so model-capability and prompt-underspecification must be separated before concluding a model class is unusable.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a detector validated only against its author's planted surface may not generalize; excluding a known volatile hop-by-hop header (Connection) is a canonical instrumentation fix, and a stability gate must test the frozen quantity, not a stricter composite.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): prerequisite chains (shipped carrier -> discriminating task bank -> capable agent) should be repaired once at the lowest responsible lane rather than rediscovered as MEASUREMENT_INVALID across multiple lanes.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): if fresh-instance acquisition cost grows with site depth there is a persistence break-even surface; if it is flat, the honest architecture treats acquisition as a constant-cost procedure and moves effort to procedure caching and substrate expansion.

allocation.question: On a stdlib-only, locally served, multi-endpoint, multi-verb HTTP application whose goal texts are authored by a process that never sees the mechanism intent strings, with a preregistered contamination screen scoring every goal against EVERY registry intent, a traceable authoring-provenance record, a reference arm that is PROVABLY distinct from the candidate, and positive / null / dynamic-range controls each of which must be shown arithmetically able to fail and live-verified before freeze: does max-cosine-similarity selection over intent embeddings bind the correct mechanism on goals never seen at authoring time, by how much above a token-overlap null, with abstention scored as its own outcome class, pooled false-accept <= 0.10, UNKNOWN precision >= 0.85 and global plus per-class ECE <= 0.15 (bootstrap 97.5% upper <= 0.18)?
allocation.rationale: The last accepted C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE packet established a bounded decomposition that makes this redesign the highest-value Graph move: the goal-to-mechanism selection signal is real (unseen paraphrase 19/20 embedding vs 15/20 lexical null; 45/52 embedding-argmax vs 52/52 internal-id oracle), but it was destroyed by an applicability gate that fired on 0 of 52 applicable goals and by a reference arm provably identical to the candidate (argmax of a monotone transform of cosine similarity). The active mandate is a design-contract-v2 rebuild that removes the joint-authorship confound, forces a distinct reference arm and makes each control capable of firing. It sits directly on the product resolve step and on readiness condition (1) for the flagship benchmark. The tunnel_flag on this lane reflects a 7/10 recent concentration on C-FRESHNESS, but that four-anchor D1V route was just parked (single-anchor, transport-coupled, degenerate clustered bound), so the lane's own frontier has already moved; the flag is stale relative to the active C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE mandate. A cognitive reset agrees: a fresh Graph seeing today's Codex would fix the proven-inert resolver, not re-run the parked freshness route.
